newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures edge higher on JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures edge higher on JGB gains.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures edged higher on the back of gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures in an otherwise featureless market on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market ignored gains in Tokyo stocks and comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita about Japan's economic recovery becoming more solid.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.39 at 1145 GMT against its IMM close at 99.37. December was at 99.27 against 99.24.
March JGBs settled at 126.70 against their previous 126.13.
Dealers said the contract was suddenly pushed up from its earlier high of 126.42 before the close by local players trying to trigger stop-loss buy orders.
"It's crazy. There were only two locals in the pit. And from 126.50 to 126.70, only three lots were traded," said a dealer with a European house.
"They were trying to create new highs so that those with stops would come in," he said.
He said the move was a freak trade and Tokyo was likely to follow the contract price set by LIFFE at Thursday's open.
"JGBs have consolidated around 126.00 for the last couple of days. They were very well bid out of Tokyo between 125.90 and 126.00," said a trader with an Asian futures house.
"Any pullback would be a good opportunity to go long," he said, adding that there was no sign of any rollover activity into the June contract as yet.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed ahead of the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for January, due at 1330 GMT.
A lower than expected Producer Price Index (PPI) last week had made players cautious about taking aggressive positions, dealers said.

"The PPI number put some pressure on people who had shorted the market. They were expecting a positive number and it turned out negative so a lot of people were caught on the wrong side," said the trader.
Economists on average expect the overall CPI to be up 0.3 percent and the core level, excluding the volatile food and energy components, to increase 0.2 percent.
